title: SSC CGL Tier 1 Sectional Test 02: General Awareness

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for the establishment and constitution of the Supreme Court of India?
questions.explanation: Article 124 of the Constitution establishes the Supreme Court of India and prescribes the appointment and qualifications of the Chief Justice and judges. (Article 214 deals with High Courts).
questions.citation: Constitution of India — Part V, Chapter IV

questions.question: The famous iron pillar near Qutub Minar in Delhi, renowned for its rust-resistant metallurgy, was erected during the reign of which Gupta emperor?
questions.explanation: The Iron Pillar of Mehrauli bears an inscription referring to a king named 'Chandra', identified by historians as Gupta ruler Chandragupta II (reigned c. 375–415 CE).
questions.citation: NCERT Class 11 Ancient History — The Gupta Golden Age

questions.question: Which of the following peninsular rivers flows westwards into the Arabian Sea through a rift valley?
questions.explanation: The Narmada and Tapti rivers flow westwards through faulted rift valleys between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges, emptying into the Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea).
questions.citation: NCERT Class 9 Geography — Chapter 3 Drainage

questions.question: In macroeconomic accounting, Gross National Product at factor cost (GNP_FC) is equal to:
options: GNP at market price minus Net Indirect Taxes (Indirect Taxes - Subsidies)
GDP at market price plus Net Indirect Taxes
NNP at factor cost plus Net Factor Income from Abroad
GDP at factor cost minus Depreciation
questions.explanation: Market Price includes Net Indirect Taxes. Therefore: Factor Cost = Market Price - Net Indirect Taxes (Taxes - Subsidies). Thus GNP_FC = GNP_MP - Net Indirect Taxes.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Macroeconomics — National Income Accounting

questions.question: What is the SI unit of electric potential difference?
questions.explanation: The SI unit of electric potential difference is the Volt (V), named after Alessandro Volta, defined as 1 Joule of work done per 1 Coulomb of charge moved (1 V = 1 J/C).
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Science — Chapter 11 Electricity

questions.question: Which of the following chemical compounds is commonly known as 'Plaster of Paris'?
questions.explanation: Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate (CaSO4 · 1/2 H2O), produced by heating gypsum (CaSO4 · 2H2O) to 373 K.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Science — Chapter 2 Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.question: Which endocrine gland in the human body is known as the 'master gland' because it regulates the secretion of hormones from other endocrine glands?
questions.explanation: The pituitary gland, located at the base of the brain beneath the hypothalamus, secretes trophic hormones (like TSH, ACTH, LH, FSH) that regulate other endocrine glands.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Science — Chapter 6 Control and Coordination

questions.question: Who was the Viceroy of India when the Indian National Congress was founded in Bombay in December 1885?
questions.explanation: Lord Dufferin served as Viceroy of India from 1884 to 1888. The Indian National Congress held its inaugural session in Bombay on December 28, 1885 under his viceroyalty.
questions.citation: Modern Indian History — Foundation of the Indian National Congress

questions.question: Sattriya, one of the 8 recognized classical dance forms of India, originated in which state?
questions.explanation: Sattriya dance originated in the 15th century in the Vaishnavite monasteries (Sattras) of Assam, founded by the great polymath and saint Mahapurusha Srimanta Sankaradeva.
questions.citation: CCRT India & Sangeet Natak Akademi — Classical Dance Forms

questions.question: Which was the first Biosphere Reserve established in India (in 1986)?
questions.explanation: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, spanning the Western Ghats across Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka, was declared India's first biosphere reserve in September 1986.
questions.citation: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change — Biosphere Reserves in India

questions.question: The Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution, popularly known as the 'Anti-Defection Law', was inserted by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
questions.explanation: The 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1985 added the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution, providing disqualification grounds on defection for legislators.
questions.citation: Constitution of India — Tenth Schedule

questions.question: Which ruler of the Delhi Sultanate introduced market control and price regulation reforms along with the 'Dagh' (branding of horses) system?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji (reigned 1296–1316) introduced stringent market control mechanisms (Shahna-i-Mandi), fixed commodity prices, and instituted the Dagh (branding of horses) and Chehra (descriptive rolls) systems.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 11 Medieval India — The Delhi Sultanate

questions.question: Which of the following taxes is a direct tax levied by the Central Government in India?
questions.explanation: Corporation Tax and Personal Income Tax are direct taxes whose liability cannot be shifted to another entity. GST, customs duties, and excise are indirect taxes.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Macroeconomics — Government Budget and the Economy

questions.question: The Ramsar Convention is an international treaty dedicated to the conservation and sustainable utilization of which ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Signed in Ramsar, Iran in 1971, the Ramsar Convention is an intergovernmental environmental treaty providing the framework for national action and international cooperation for wetland conservation.
questions.citation: Ramsar Convention on Wetlands — International Environmental Agreements

questions.question: Which high mountain pass connects the Kashmir Valley with the Union Territory of Ladakh through the Zaskar Range?
questions.explanation: Zoji La Pass (altitude ~3,528 m) on National Highway 1 connects Srinagar in the Kashmir Valley to Kargil and Leh in Ladakh.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 11 India Physical Environment — Mountain Passes

questions.question: Deficiency of Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) causes which of the following diseases characterized by bleeding gums and delayed wound healing?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C is essential for collagen synthesis. Its deficiency causes scurvy (bleeding gums, petechiae, joint pains). Rickets is caused by Vitamin D deficiency, Beriberi by B1, and Pellagra by B3.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Science — Human Nutrition

questions.question: On the recommendation of which Committee were Fundamental Duties incorporated into Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution in 1976?
questions.explanation: The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended the inclusion of Fundamental Duties, which led to the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act inserting Article 51A under Part IV-A.
questions.citation: Constitution of India — Part IV-A Article 51A

questions.question: Where is the headquarters of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) located?
questions.explanation: The International Court of Justice (principal judicial organ of the UN) is seated at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands.
questions.citation: United Nations System — Principal Organs

questions.question: The Treaty of Salbai (1782) brought an end to which Anglo-Maratha conflict?
questions.explanation: Signed on 17 May 1782 between the British East India Company (Warren Hastings) and Mahadji Shinde, the Treaty of Salbai concluded the First Anglo-Maratha War, establishing 20 years of mutual peace.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 11 Modern India — Anglo-Maratha Wars

questions.question: In which medium does sound travel with the highest velocity at 25°C?
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical longitudinal wave requiring elastic matter to propagate. Because solids have the highest elastic bulk modulus and density coupling, sound travels fastest in solid metals (~6,420 m/s in aluminium), followed by liquids (~1,498 m/s in water), gases (~346 m/s in air), and 0 m/s in vacuum.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 9 Science — Chapter 12 Sound

questions.question: Which prerogative writ is issued by the Supreme Court or High Court to compel a public official or body to perform a statutory duty that they have failed to execute?
questions.explanation: The writ of Mandamus (meaning 'We Command') is issued to secure the performance of a public or statutory duty that an official, public authority, or lower tribunal is bound by law to perform.
questions.citation: Constitution of India — Article 32 & Article 226

questions.question: Which price index is used by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) as the official headline anchor for monetary policy formulation and inflation targeting?
questions.explanation: Following the recommendations of the Urjit Patel Committee in 2014, the RBI officially adopted the Consumer Price Index Combined (CPI-C) with a flexible inflation target of 4% (+/- 2%).
questions.citation: Reserve Bank of India Monetary Policy Framework

questions.question: Which planet in our solar system has the shortest orbital period around the Sun (88 Earth days)?
questions.explanation: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun (semi-major axis ~0.387 AU) and completes an orbital revolution in approximately 87.97 Earth days.
questions.citation: Physical Geography — Planetary Motions

questions.question: The renowned treatise on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy titled 'Arthashastra' is traditionally attributed to:
questions.explanation: The Arthashastra was authored by Kautilya (Vishnugupta / Chanakya), prime minister to Chandragupta Maurya in the 4th century BCE.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Indian History — Early States and Economies

questions.question: What is the chemical name of common baking soda?
questions.explanation: Baking soda is Sodium Hydrogen Carbonate (NaHCO3). Washing soda is Na2CO3·10H2O, caustic soda is NaOH, and bleaching powder is CaOCl2.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Science — Chapter 2 Baking Soda
